titulo: No sé vs no lo sé = I don't know
regla: As an immediate reply to a question, both no sé and no lo sé work (no sé is more casual, no lo sé a bit firmer). When it isn't a direct reply, or the thing not known comes later or is spelled out, you need lo or an object: No lo sé todavía, ya te diré. Before a question word, no lo: No sé dónde está.

lista.texto: **No sé** or **No lo sé**: both fine. **Lo** = what was just asked.

lista.forma: not a direct reply / with more after
lista.texto: Use **lo**: **Pues no lo sé, tengo que revisar.**
No **lo**: **no sé dónde vive**, **no sé si viene**.

bloques.texto: **No sé** alone can also be a filler, like _I dunno, kind of_: **Está, no sé, raro.**
Same with **no lo creo, no lo entiendo** vs **no creo, no entiendo**.
Tip: if the sentence keeps going with **qué, dónde, si...**, drop the **lo**.

lista.en: —That actor's name is Ricardo, right? —I don't know.

lista.es: —¿Se te antoja ir por unos tacos? —==No lo sé==, no tengo mucha hambre.
lista.en: —Do you feel like getting tacos? —I don't know, I'm not very hungry.

lista.es: —¿Cómo se escribe esa palabra? —Déjame ver... pues ==no lo sé==.
lista.en: —How do you spell that word? —Let me see... well, I don't know.
I don't know where I left the keys.

lista.es: ==No sé si== voy a poder ir.
lista.en: I don't know if I'll be able to go.
The movie was, I dunno, weird.

lista.nota: The question word is the object; no **lo**.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I don't know what time it starts._
lista.r: No sé a qué hora empieza.

lista.p: Reply after thinking: _Hmm... no, I don't know._
Fix it: _No lo sé si viene._
